title: Content-address serialization depends on object insertion order
reasoning: canonicalJson is documented as the deterministic serialization used for content-addressing, but JSON.stringify preserves object insertion order for non-integer keys. Two semantically identical SpreadsheetModel values with the same cells inserted in different orders, or nested CellValue objects with different construction order, can serialize differently and therefore hash to different content addresses. That creates false snapshot churn and breaks deduplication/change detection based on the canonical string.
reproduction: Construct two spreadsheet models with cells { A1: { v: 'x' }, B1: { v: 'y' } } and { B1: { v: 'y' }, A1: { v: 'x' } }; canonicalJson returns strings with different cell key order even though the model content is the same.
recommendation: Implement canonical serialization that recursively sorts object keys before stringifying, or store ordered arrays for map-like data before content-addressing.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for this feature, and there is no evidence of a regression test that compares canonicalJson output for equivalent models constructed with different key insertion orders.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that builds equivalent DocModel instances with reversed object insertion order for spreadsheet cells and asserts canonicalJson returns identical strings.
minimumFixScope: Update canonicalJson in packages/core/src/model/types.ts to normalize object key order recursively and add focused tests for map ordering.
